bibliographic.title: Large Language Models in Finance: A Survey
bibliographic.authors: Yinheng Li; Shaofei Wang; Han Ding; Hang Chen
bibliographic.citation_apa: Li, Y., Wang, S., Ding, H., & Chen, H. (2024). Large Language Models in Finance: A Survey [Preprint]. Columbia University; New York University.

methodology.technology_context: LLMs for financial applications including zero-shot/few-shot use of pretrained models, fine-tuning on domain-specific data, training custom LLMs, and financial NLP tasks; mentions ChatGPT and customer service among finance use cases

eligibility.decision_rationale: The provided text identifies a finance-focused LLM survey with adoption guidance, risks, and responsible-use framing in a regulated sector, but does not center conversational systems, governance mechanisms such as guardrails, audit, tracing, human oversight, or accountability in chatbot/agent deployments.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only page 1/front matter was supplied; later sections on risks, limitations, and the decision framework may contain additional governance-relevant content not visible in the excerpt.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is constrained to page 1. Objectives are clearly stated as a practical survey of LLM solutions and adoption guidance for finance, but review methodology, literature search strategy, inclusion criteria, and analytical procedures are not described in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: The excerpt supports relevance to regulated finance and general responsible LLM adoption, but provides insufficient detail on review methods and little direct evidence on conversational governance, oversight, auditability, or compliance controls.

coding.subtheme: decision guidance and responsible use in regulated finance

synthesis.main_claim: The paper surveys current LLM approaches for finance and proposes a decision framework to help financial professionals choose appropriate LLM solutions based on data, compute, and performance constraints, while also discussing limitations, challenges, and responsible application.
synthesis.contribution: Synthesizes finance-oriented LLM solution patterns and offers a staged adoption pathway from lightweight experimentation to customized LLM investment in a regulated industry context.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text does not describe the survey's literature selection method or evidence base; governance topics relevant to conversational systems are not evidenced in the excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for LLM deployment and adoption considerations in regulated finance, not as central evidence on conversational governance, operational controls, or human oversight mechanisms.
